title: Sir Edward Stafford (Paris) to Sir Francis Walsingham, 19 September 1586 (BL Harley MS 1582 ff. 74-75; DECODE R8503)

plaintext.source: Contemporary decipherment written above each of the four cipher runs on f. 74v.

transcription.notes: Four short runs transcribed sign by sign with their interlinear glosses; the clear text was read for context, not transcribed in full.

system.summary: Graphic-sign and letter-form alphabet with homophones and a null, plus two-digit codes for persons (47 King of Navarre, 59 Prince of Conde, 74 Duke of Guise).
system.notes: Stafford's cipher with Walsingham; no key sheet found. Letter values rebuilt here from the glosses.

prior_solution.where: Interlinear decipherment on f. 74v; not in CSP Foreign XXI pt 1 (Harley MS, outside the State Papers)

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up the coding agent with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched the DECODE record, its API metadata and the 4 full-resolution images with the session cookie.
Read the pages: holograph clear despatch, Paris 19 Sept 1586, addressed on f. 75v to Walsingham; cipher only in four short runs on f. 74v, each glossed above.
CSP Foreign XXI pt 1, September 1586, 16-30 (BHO pp. 89-104): Stafford's SP letters of that month calendared, this Harley letter not; cryptiana Elizabethan page: no Stafford-Walsingham key.
Transcribed the four runs sign by sign with their glosses (Villequier; K. Navar; Kyll him and ye P. of Conde; D. Guise).
First try: the gloss 'villequier' covers only the six line-end signs; did not fit ten letters.
Run 1 read as one run across the line break with 6 as null: D x ◇ ◇ Δ Ɗ X ⊕ ꟻ ʃ = v i l l e q u i e r; run 3 M x ◇ h = k y l l with the same x and ◇ and 6 again null; 47/59/74 name codes.

outcome.notes: Read at the time; all four runs re-read sign by sign and the letter values rebuilt (partial alphabet, three name codes, null 6). DECODE recipient 'unknown' is Walsingham; place is Paris.
